# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

**Qi2** is the open wireless charging standard from the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC) that added a magnetic ring and a 15W cap. The magnets align the phone and charger, which improves efficiency and charging speed. It's based on Apple's MagSafe tech ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey), [WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**Qi2.2** is the newer version of that standard, marketed as **"Qi2 25W."** It raises the cap to 25W, nearly 70% more power than Qi2. The WPC says it can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes. The first certified products appeared in July 2025 ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/), [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**MagSafe** is Apple's own branding and technology: a ring of magnets around the iPhone's charging coil that snaps compatible accessories into the best charging position. Apple's current MagSafe Charger is certified for Qi2 25W, so MagSafe and Qi2 are largely interchangeable for iPhone users. It also falls back to regular Qi for an iPhone 8 or later at 7.5W ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m), [Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)).

## What speed you actually get
Your phone sets the limit, not just the charger. Per [Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047), with a 30W or greater adapter:

| iPhone | Max wireless speed |
|---|---|
| 17 series, 18 Pro/Pro Max, 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max | 25W |
| 16, 16 Pro | 22.5W |
| iPhone Air | 20W |
| 17e, 15 and earlier | 15W |

Using USB-C or Lightning accessories while charging lowers these speeds.

**Android:** Support is thin. According to [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks), the Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold support Qi2 at 15W, and the Pixel 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2 at 25W. Samsung's Galaxy lineup is "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case for full function.

## Which to buy
Any Qi2-certified charger works with MagSafe iPhones, and Qi2.2 chargers work with older phones at their lower speeds. For 25W, look for the **Qi2 25W** logo. Only certified products can display the Qi or Qi2 logo ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

If you want a simple option, Apple's [MagSafe Charger (2 m), $49](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m) is certified for Qi2 25W. You'll need a 30W USB-C adapter, which is sold separately, to reach 25W.
